### CANDIDATE DETAIL
#### 1. tooth agenesis, selective, 9  —  Tier 3 — Moderate / Emerging  (fitness 0.398)
**Link type:** shared pathway (Reactome:R-HSA-201451)

**Proposed mechanism:** CHRDL1 (HGNC:2303) —DISRUPTS→ BMP signaling pathway (REACT:R-HSA-5690675); GREM2 (HGNC:14716) —DISRUPTS→ BMP signaling pathway (REACT:R-HSA-5690675); BMP signaling pathway (REACT:R-HSA-5690675) —LEADS_TO→ Megalocornea (HP:0000500); BMP signaling pathway (REACT:R-HSA-5690675) —LEADS_TO→ Selective tooth agenesis (HP:0000177). Loss-of-function mutations in either CHRDL1 or GREM2 disrupt the BMP signaling pathway. Aberrant BMP signaling subsequently leads to developmental defects manifesting as megalocornea in the eye and tooth agenesis in the dentition.

**How to falsify it:** Identification of pathogenic variants in CHRDL1 or GREM2 that do not demonstrably disrupt BMP signaling in cellular or animal models, or discovery of distinct, non-overlapping molecular pathways causative for each disease. _(variant: Presence of common benign variants in CHRDL1 or GREM2 in gnomAD with frequencies > 1% that are associated with either phenotype.)_

**Why it matters:** Understanding the shared role of CHRDL1 and GREM2 in BMP signaling could reveal common therapeutic targets for developmental disorders affecting craniofacial and ocular structures. Modulating BMP signaling might offer a unified approach to treating aspects of these conditions.

#### 2. brachydactyly type A2  —  Tier 3 — Moderate / Emerging  (fitness 0.384)
**Link type:** shared pathway (Reactome:R-HSA-201451)

**Proposed mechanism:** CHRDL1 (HGNC:2446) —DECREASES→ BMP signaling pathway (P00018); BMP signaling pathway (P00018) —LEADS_TO→ Isolated congenital megalocornea (HP:0000559); BMP2 (HGNC:1224) —INCREASES→ BMP signaling pathway (P00018); BMPR1B (HGNC:1230) —INCREASES→ BMP signaling pathway (P00018); GDF5 (HGNC:4219) —INCREASES→ BMP signaling pathway (P00018); BMP signaling pathway (P00018) —LEADS_TO→ Brachydactyly type A2 (HP:0005825). CHRDL1 is an antagonist of BMP signaling. Haploinsufficiency of CHRDL1 leads to increased BMP signaling, contributing to megalocornea. BMP2, BMPR1B, and GDF5 are components of the BMP signaling pathway. Haploinsufficiency in these genes disrupts proper BMP signaling, leading to brachydactyly type A2. Both diseases converge on a shared dysregulation of the BMP signaling pathway, albeit through different mechanisms (antagonist vs. signaling components).

**How to falsify it:** Demonstration that mutations in CHRDL1 do not affect BMP signaling, or that mutations in BMP2, BMPR1B, or GDF5 do not impact skeletal development. _(variant: gnomAD v2.1.1 non_cancer AF for pathogenic variants in CHRDL1, BMP2, BMPR1B, GDF5 exceeding 0.01%)_

**Why it matters:** Understanding the shared role of BMP signaling in these distinct conditions could reveal novel therapeutic targets for both ocular and skeletal developmental disorders.

Separately, mutations in BMP2 also disrupt the BMP signaling pathway, leading to a spectrum of skeletal and facial anomalies, as well as short stature.
